reflexion_entries_to_archive.entry: Applying doc corrections via `python -c "..."` inside a bash command let the shell perform command substitution on every backticked identifier in my markdown payload, silently deleting `pickTargetSpark`, `BotGoal`, `serializeSpawner` and ~20 more from 3 lines while REPORTING '4 of 5 applied'. The success count was true and the content was corrupt. Two compounding lessons: (1) for any payload containing backticks, braces or quotes, write a script FILE with the Write tool and execute that - never inline it through a shell; (2) an 'applied N/N' report from my own script is not verification of CONTENT, only of substring matching, so I wrote scan_damage.py to hunt the damage signature (odd backtick counts, doubled spaces, bare empty parens) rather than trusting the counter. I had already hit a heredoc quoting failure earlier in the same session and switched to files once; I regressed to `python -c` two steps later.

My first production-stripping check was `if grep -rl NEEDLE dist/ | grep -v map | head -3; then echo LEAKED; else echo ABSENT; fi`. It printed LEAKED for all three needles with no filenames - because `head` always exits 0, so the `if` ALWAYS took the then-branch. The check could not have reported ABSENT for any input, including a genuinely clean bundle. Rewritten to COUNT files (`grep -l ... | grep -cv '\.map$'`), which then showed 0/0/0. Rule: a verification whose verdict comes from a pipeline's exit status is testing the LAST command, not the predicate. Make the check produce a NUMBER and assert on the number. Corollary that saved me here: I only doubted the result because it disagreed with the +114 B delta I expected - a cross-check from an independent measurement is what exposed the broken instrument.

The bundle after my change was 656300 B against an audit-reported 656186 B baseline. I could have called that 'unchanged' or 'noise'. Instead I moved src/dev aside, git-checkout-ed main.ts, and rebuilt: the baseline reproduced EXACTLY at 656186 B (hash BD5X8Lx1), making the delta a precise +114 B rather than an estimate. That matters because the PDR's headline claim was 'zero production change', and the honest number is 'the harness logic is stripped; a 114-byte empty module record for the side-effect bootstrap import remains'. GROK's R2 attack on that exact claim ('false marketing') was wrong on the mechanism but right to demand the measurement.

Synthetic pointer events on the Pixi canvas did nothing and an async rAF-awaiting script timed out at 30s. Root cause: with the Browser pane not displayed the page does not composite, so rAF never fires and the Pixi ticker - which drives the entire sim loop - does not advance. Static DOM reads (overlay text, window globals, the lambda override) still work fine, which is why the first checks succeeded and misled me into trying clicks. So: DOM/global assertions are available with a hidden pane; anything requiring a FRAME is not. When the game loop is needed and the pane is unavailable, drop to the reducer level - the contract test I wrote instead is deterministic, permanent regression coverage, and strictly better evidence than one browser click would have been.

I ran the S126-S150 -> V6-x.y relabel and the factual corrections in one script, relabel first. That ordering was load-bearing and I nearly got it backwards: several corrections ADD genuine references to the real S126 and S127 (e.g. 'already retired in S126'), and had they landed before the regex pass those true historical references would have been rewritten into V6 slot labels - a silent corruption that greps clean. The header substitution did fail for exactly this reason (its source string still contained 'S126 -> S150', already rewritten), which surfaced the hazard cheaply. Rule: mechanical renames run BEFORE any edit that introduces new instances of the old token, and the rename regex must be range-restricted (S126-S150 only) so historical refs survive.

B4 (does a capped exact-type bank destroy the carve-down tactic?) nearly escaped twice. First at DESIGN: my original probe gave free material under carry-1, which forces the old behaviour and can only illustrate starvation - both Council legs caught that independently. Then at IMPLEMENTATION: the redesigned probe's metric compared owned-primitive COUNTS, so a placement and a sever in the same 250ms window cancelled to zero and carving was systematically under-reported - GEMINI-AUDITOR caught that in CHECK, GROK missed it. Same question, two layers, two near-misses, both caught by an adversarial reviewer rather than by me. The transferable lesson: when an artifact's PURPOSE is to measure something, audit the measurement path as a first-class deliverable - I verified that the harness ran, was stripped, and typechecked, but not that its counters could distinguish the two outcomes it existed to distinguish. 'Does it work?' and 'can it tell the difference?' are different questions.

check_result: TRIUMVIRATE (Full tier): RALPH:PATROL + GROK-ANALYST + GEMINI-AUDITOR on the raw P2 diff, plus 47/47 scripted doc checks for P1. Six findings CONFIRMED and fixed; one REFUTED empirically. The decisive one was GEMINI-AUDITOR's, missed by GROK: net-change aliasing meant the B4 metric could not have measured B4 - comparing owned-primitive COUNTS makes a placement and a sever in the same sampling window cancel to nothing, biasing toward UNDER-reporting carving, which is exactly the false negative that would have wrongly confirmed B4. Fixed with a set difference (diffOwned), pinned by 3 new tests. Also fixed: prevPrimCount starting at 0; the harness silently breaking under ?worker=1 (verified: SPAWN_SPARK is absent from CLIENT_INTENT_TYPES_RECORD while PICKUP_SPARK: true is present, so the spawn intent would be dropped and the pickup would reference a nonexistent spark); a solo-gate race between the 250ms sampler and a keypress; fixed-base probe ids; HMR accumulation of overlays/timers/listeners. REFUTED: GEMINI elevated to HIGH a claim that a failed ?spawn= override would make the overlay falsely report OVERRIDDEN - the displayed value is the imported constant, not the URL param, so it displays the true 0.1875. The underlying worry was still actioned via a requested-vs-observed mismatch warning. ACCEPTED AS PROCEDURAL: regime toggle cannot reset the world, so the overlay now warns when primitives predate a counter reset and tells the owner to restart the match for a clean A/B. analyze_result:
CALIBRATION. Estimate was ~52K across two priorities; actual close is ~478K context at session end, but that number is dominated by the A.0 sweep (1.9M subagent tokens across 11 agents) and the 2-round Council, neither of which the PDR's token line was scoped to cover. The EDIT work itself landed close to estimate. Lesson for future Full-tier PDRs in this project: state the deliberation+audit budget separately from the implementation budget, because they differ by an order of magnitude and conflating them makes the estimate meaningless.

WHAT THE DELIBERATION ACTUALLY BOUGHT, measured rather than assumed. Council R1 killed the original P2 design outright: both legs independently observed that free material under carry-1 forces the OLD behaviour and so could only have illustrated B3 starvation, never tested B4. Had I shipped the first design, the owner would have playtested an instrument incapable of answering the question it was built for. Then the CHECK phase caught that even the REDESIGNED instrument had a metric that could not measure B4 (count-delta aliasing). So the same blocker was nearly missed twice, at two different layers - design, then implementation - and was caught both times by an adversarial reviewer rather than by me. That is the strongest evidence this session produced for keeping Triumvirate CHECK mandatory on Full tier.

REVIEWER CALIBRATION. GROK: 6 findings, 3 refuted on empirical grounds (the no-new-action-type objection, a bundle-charter conflation, and a scope error about gatherers that do not exist yet). It also attacked my risk-placement proposal and then prescribed almost exactly the same thing. GEMINI: fewer findings, higher hit rate, and it found the one defect that mattered most - but it also fabricated a mechanism (claiming the overlay reads the URL when it reads the imported constant) and elevated that fabrication to HIGH. Pattern confirmed for the third session running: reviewer findings must be grep-verified against the code before triage, and the correct response to a fabricated mechanism is to fix the underlying worry anyway when it is cheap.

PROCESS FAILURES, both mine, both self-caught. (1) A `python -c` payload through bash let the shell command-substitute every backticked identifier out of 3 markdown lines while reporting '4 of 5 applied' - a true success count over corrupt content. I had already hit heredoc quoting failure earlier in the same session and switched to script files once, then regressed two steps later. (2) My first production-stripping check was structurally incapable of reporting a pass, because `head` won the pipeline's exit status. I only doubted it because it disagreed with an independent measurement. Both are logged as reflexion; the second generalises to a rule worth promoting - a verification whose verdict comes from a pipeline's exit status is testing the last command, not the predicate, so make it produce a NUMBER and assert on the number.

WHAT DID NOT GET DONE, explicitly. Nothing is pushed: the GitHub token is invalid and Git Credential Manager hangs on an invisible prompt, so 8 commits and the v0.5.2-pre-pivot tag are local only. That also blocks the Pages build_type flip and any CI dispatch, so the e2e gating lane was NOT run this session (unit suite and build stand in). Live gameplay was not exercised in-browser either, because a hidden Browser pane pauses requestAnimationFrame and the Pixi ticker never advances; substituted reducer-level contract tests, which are better evidence anyway. The owner's playtest - the actual instrument for B3/B4 - remains outstanding and is the gate on V6-1.3/V6-1.4.

SHAPE OF THE REMAINING RISK. The pivot's 23 catalogued risks are now bound to the slots that must clear them, but three deserve early attention because they invert planned ordering rather than merely complicating it: R6 (no damageable target exists, so 3 of 5 targeting priorities would be dead UI - V6-2.1 must move or a structure-HP slot must precede it), R5 (WIN_TRIGGER destroys 7 entity families at t=0, so whether a castle survives the 28s ceremony is a V6-1.2 decision, not a V6-3.1 one), and R12 (the host sends the full payload once per active transport strategy and 10Hz is a cap that was measured collapsing to 2.2Hz, so delta encoding is Phase-1-adjacent rather than V6-4.2 cleanup).
